newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slightly weaker, spread focus.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slightly weaker, spread focus.

text.p: Price movements remained narrow on the white sugar futures market on Monday afternoon as interest to trade the nearby December/March spread boosted total volume.
Activity was dull earlier in the session as the market got off to a slow start to the week and nearby values showed little inclination to rise too far above opening levels.
But then the volume was boosted by broker and commission house selling of the spread and some crosses were also seen, traders said.
"I don't think anyone has stood out as buying it or selling it, it's just a mixed bag," said one trader.

Last week the second-month March contract took over the main market interest when open interest overtook that of December. Some outright March trades were also reported and the position accounted for the bulk of the overall volume.
"I think most of the December that has been traded today is via the switch," the trader said.
At 1526 GMT December stood 20 cents lower at $321.90 and March down 40 cents at $317.70. Volume amounted to 1,927 lots.
In physical news, Syria tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws for shipment between November 25 and December 25.
November 5 is set as the final date to receive bids and the results of the tender are to be announced on November 6.
Paris activity was lacklustre with only three contracts trading.
December was down 40 cents at $322.00 and March down 90 cents at $317.80. Matif volume totalled 434 lots.
